name: r3_relevance_question
rationale: Failures like dev-0216 (relevant=1) and dev-0294 give a generic developing description that misses the specific point a strong player would ask about, so forcing the model to answer why-here/why-now/what-does-it-give-up should lift the weakest axis (relevance 3.00) without touching the hedging that already fixed faithfulness.
instruction:
Before writing, work through the position silently: identify the piece that moved, its origin and destination square, and what it now attacks, defends, or opens up -- check each claim against the actual diagram, not memory. Then ask yourself the question a strong player would ask about this exact move: why here, why now, and what square, file, tempo, or structure does it give up to get it. Do not show this reasoning or use headers.

Write 1-4 plain sentences in the voice of a human annotator noting their own game -- ordinary prose, no markdown, no bold, no bullets, no hype adjectives, no generic filler that would fit any position. Your sentences must answer the question above, not just describe the move happening. Prefer plans, ideas, and evaluations over concrete tactical claims. Name at most one concrete threat -- a specific piece taking a specific square next move -- and only if verified on this board; otherwise mention none. Never say who stands better unless material makes it obvious. If nothing concrete and verified stands out, write one short, modest sentence answering the why-here-why-now question anyway. Output only the commentary.

name: r3_zero_threat_structure_only
rationale: Several overall<=2 items (dev-0127, dev-0151, dev-0219, dev-0286) hallucinate a pin or attack that the current 'one verified threat' rule doesn't police since it only covers next-move capture claims, so banning pin/attack language outright and restricting evaluation to structure/activity/king-safety words should close that gap.
instruction:
Before writing, work through the position silently: identify the piece that moved, its origin and destination square, and what it now attacks, defends, or opens up -- check each claim against the actual diagram, not memory. Do not show this reasoning or use headers.

Write 1-4 plain sentences in the voice of a human annotator noting their own game -- ordinary prose, no markdown, no bold, no bullets, no hype adjectives, no generic filler that would fit any position. Describe the position only through pawn structure, piece activity, and king safety -- which squares are weak, which pieces are well or badly placed, whose king is safer -- not through claims about pins, forks, attacks, or threats. Name no concrete threat, pin, or attack of any kind unless it is a capture or check literally available this move on this board; if so you may name that one, otherwise name none at all. Never say who stands better unless material makes it obvious. If nothing concrete and verified stands out, write one short, modest sentence about structure or safety instead. Output only the commentary.

name: r3_phase_register
rationale: The winner's register works but applies the same recipe regardless of game phase; matching the sentence type to phase (system/plan in the opening, plan+one threat in the middlegame, king/pawn talk in the endgame) should better match what human annotators actually write per phase.
instruction:
Before writing, work through the position silently: identify the piece that moved, its origin and destination square, and what it now attacks, defends, or opens up -- check each claim against the actual diagram, not memory. Also judge the game phase from the move number and pieces on the board: opening (most pieces still home, under roughly 12 moves), middlegame (pieces developed, queens and several minors/rooks on), or endgame (few pieces left, kings active). Do not show this reasoning or use headers.

Write 1-4 plain sentences in the voice of a human annotator noting their own game -- ordinary prose, no markdown, no bold, no bullets, no hype adjectives, no generic filler. In the opening, write one sentence naming the system or plan the move fits into. In the middlegame, name the plan and at most one concrete, verified threat -- a specific piece taking a specific square next move. In the endgame, talk only about king activity and pawn structure -- passed pawns, king proximity, weaknesses. Never say who stands better unless material makes it obvious. Output only the commentary.

name: r3_honest_cost_check
rationale: A distinct cluster of failures (dev-0078, dev-0080, dev-0167, dev-0294, all wrong-eval or misses-point) has the model narrate a confident, comfortable plan even when the reference shows the move was a blunder or already lost/won the game, so adding an explicit hanging-piece/king-safety check and letting tone follow it honestly should stop that reflexive positive spin.
instruction:
Before writing, work through the position silently: identify the piece that moved, its origin and destination square, and what it now attacks, defends, or opens up -- check each claim against the actual diagram, not memory. Also check, honestly, whether this move left anything of the mover's own hanging or undefended, and whether the mover's king is now more or less safe than before -- do not assume the move worked out well. Do not show this reasoning or use headers.

Write 1-4 plain sentences in the voice of a human annotator noting their own game -- ordinary prose, no markdown, no bold, no bullets, no hype adjectives, no generic filler. Let your tone follow what you actually verified: if the move costs something or leaves the mover worse off, say so plainly instead of describing a comfortable plan. Prefer plans and evaluations over concrete tactical claims. Name at most one concrete threat -- a specific piece taking a specific square next move -- and only if verified; otherwise name none. Never say who stands better unless material makes it obvious. Output only the commentary.
